Article Title: Ramaiah Group expands its educational legacy with the inauguration of RISM, foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya
Article Text:
Dignitaries at the inauguration of the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management and foundation-laying ceremony for Nareyana Pragnalaya in Bengaluru.

Ramaiah legacy of building a knowledge society

RISM: Global knowledge meets technology

Academic and institutional leaders gathered at the Ramaiah Group event marking the launch of RISM and the foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya.

Nareyana Pragnalaya – ‘Abode of Wisdom’

As India continues to strengthen its position as a knowledge-driven economy, institutions of higher learning are playing an increasingly important role in shaping future-ready talent, advancing research and fostering innovation. Reflecting this vision, the Ramaiah Group of Institutions’ longstanding contribution to education and nation-building came into focus in Bengaluru today, as D.K. Shivakumar, Chief Minister of Karnataka, inaugurated the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management (RISM) and laid the foundation stone for Nareyana Pragnalaya: ‘Abode of Wisdom’, recognising the Group’s significant role in building a knowledge society in India.The ceremony marked an important milestone in the Ramaiah Group’s continuing journey in education and brought together eminent academic and institutional leaders, including Dr. M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM; Dr. Seetharam, Chairman, Gokula Education Foundation; Dr. Havidan Rodríguez, President, University at Albany, State University of New York; Dr. M.M. Pallam Raju, Member, Board of Management; Prof. B.N. Raghunandan, Chairman, RISM Task Force; and Gurucharan Gollarkeri, IAS (Retd.), Chief Strategy Officer, GEF (Medical), among others.Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appreciated the contribution of the Ramaiah Group of Institutions to education and the development of Bengaluru and Karnataka. He highlighted the role played by the institutions in creating generations of professionals, entrepreneurs and leaders and in contributing to the building of a knowledge-driven society.He also emphasised the importance of educational institutions preparing young people not merely to seek employment, but to become entrepreneurs, innovators and job creators who can contribute meaningfully to the country’s future.Dr. M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM, highlighted the vision behind the new institution and its focus on global academic engagement, research, innovation and emerging technologies.A key pillar of RISM’s academic vision is its collaboration with the University at Albany, State University of New York. The partnership is intended to provide students with access to global academic expertise, knowledge, research and emerging technologies, while creating opportunities for international exposure and industry-relevant learning.The collaboration brings together the educational legacy of the Ramaiah Group and the global academic strengths of the University at Albany, creating an environment designed to prepare students for a rapidly changing world.Dr. Jayaram also highlighted the significance of Nareyana Pragnalaya, the name given to the new RISM campus for which the foundation stone was laid.Nareyana Pragnalaya means ‘Abode of Wisdom’ and envisions a transformative space where knowledge becomes wisdom, learning inspires discovery, and education shapes enlightened minds.Rooted in timeless values and driven by a vision for tomorrow, the campus is envisioned to nurture intellect, creativity, character and compassion, empowering generations to learn, lead and shape a better world.The foundation laying therefore represents more than the creation of a new campus. It marks the beginning of a new academic environment where knowledge, technology, research and human values come together.The inauguration of the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management and the foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya – ‘Abode of Wisdom’, mark a significant milestone in the continuing educational journey of the Ramaiah Group of Institutions and Gokula Education Foundation.Building on a legacy of contributing to India’s knowledge society, the new initiatives reflect a vision of education that brings together global academic collaboration, emerging technologies, research and innovation, while remaining rooted in the values of wisdom, character and social responsibility. Together, they signal a continued commitment to nurturing future-ready generations equipped not only to navigate a changing world, but also to contribute meaningfully to its future.
Article Summary: Chief Minister of Karnataka, D.K. Shivakumar, inaugurated the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management (RISM) and laid the foundation stone for Nareyana Pragnalaya: ‘Abode of Wisdom’ Dr M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM, highlighted the vision behind the new institution and its focus on global academic engagement, research, innovation and emerging technologies.

Article Title: Srijan Realty launches Orizon, an 8.3-Acre landmark redefining residential living on Kolkata’s Southern EM Bypass

As Kolkata’s residential landscape continues to evolve, emerging micro-markets are gaining prominence as homebuyers increasingly seek a combination of connectivity, convenience and well-developed social infrastructure. The Southern EM Bypass corridor, in particular, has witnessed a decade-long transformation from a peripheral suburb into one of the city’s most aspirational residential addresses, supported by expanding metro and suburban rail connectivity, dual EM Bypass access, and a maturing ecosystem of schools, hospitals and retail destinations. Against this backdrop, Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, today announced the launch of Orizon, a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata.Located on B.C. Roy Road in Jagaddal, with two access points off the Southern EM Bypass roughly 400 metres and 750 metres apart, Orizon comprises six high-rise towers ranging from 17 to 23 storeys, housing 702 three-bedroom residences sized between approximately 1,208 and 1,650 square feet. Roughly 80 percent of the 8.3-acre site — 85 percent including podium-level landscaping, has been kept open, an unusually low-density ratio for a development of this scale so close to the city. Shahid Khudiram Metro Station is roughly14 minutes away, with Sonarpur railway station around 15 minutes; Spencer’s, Wood Square Mall and Southwinds Galleria are all within a six-minute drive.Orizon’s design philosophy takes its name from the word “horizon,” built around the idea that space, light and an unobstructed view are increasingly scarce commodities in a city that has grown denser over the past two decades. Residences feature terrace-style and standing balconies intended to maximise natural light and cross-ventilation, while the project’s golden façade, visible from the EM Bypass — is conceived as a visual landmark along the corridor.Despite its dual EM Bypass access and proximity to South Kolkata’s commercial nodes, the development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors. Schools including BDM International and Narayana, along with healthcare providers such as Apollo Hospital’s upcoming campus, Peerless Hospital and RN Tagore Hospital, are within a 20-minute radius.At the centre of the development sits a roughly 33,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring an infinity-edge swimming pool, jacuzzi and dedicated kids’ pool, alongside a 21,000-square-foot podium-level garden anchoring a sports arena with facilities for tennis, basketball, pickleball and badminton. Indoor offerings extend to a gymnasium, yoga and meditation studio, squash court, co-working space, home theatre, library, and a dedicated senior citizens’ lounge, amenities the developer says are designed to serve every age group within a single community rather than cater narrowly to one demographic.A defining feature of Orizon is its barrier-free design, incorporating wheelchair access ramps, lift cabins wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs, Braille and voice-enabled lift controls, accessible toilets and designated accessible parking throughout common areas. Srijan Realty positions this not as a regulatory minimum but as a forward-looking response to India’s multigenerational households, where ageing parents, differently abled family members and young children increasingly share a single home and require equal, independent access to shared spaces.Orizon has been pre-certified for IGBC Platinum design, India’s highest green building rating, with features including rainwater harvesting, solar power for common areas, low-flow water fixtures, energy-efficient LED lighting, organic waste management, and EV charging infrastructure. Buildings certified to this standard typically deliver 20 to 30 percent energy savings and 30 to 50 percent water savings compared with conventional construction."Orizon reflects how we believe Kolkata wants to live today. Homebuyers are no longer choosing between space and connectivity, or between design and responsibility - they expect all of it together. Southern EM Bypass has moved past being an emerging corridor - it is now one of South Kolkata's defining growth engines, and we have been part of that story for over a decade.We have built Orizon as a community first, planned around low-density living, open space, and lifestyle infrastructure that we believe will hold its value well beyond the next market cycle, with inclusivity and sustainability designed into its foundations rather than added on at the end”, said Dinesh Agarwal, Director, Srijan Realty, reflecting on the vision behind the project.Rera number: Phase I - WBRERA/P/SOU/2026/004474 |NOTE: The information contained herein is indicative and for promotional purposes. The developer reserves the right to modify any features, offerings, specifications or timelines subject to relevant authority approvals. Project visuals are artist impressions. RERA registration details available at [insert RERA number]. Prospective buyers are advised to review all legal and regulatory documentation before making investment decisions.
Article Summary: Orizon is a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata. The development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors. Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, is the developer.

Article Title: NSE IPO listing: National Stock Exchange of India to debut on September 24; check GMP & other details
Article Text:
The Rs 22,562 crore public issue consisted entirely of an offer for sale (OFS).

NSE IPO subscription

NSE IPO GMP Today

About NSE

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

NSE IPO listing: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is set to debut on the stock market on September 24, 2026. The shares are scheduled to begin trading on the BSE. With the listing now just a day away, the grey market is indicating a premium of about 2.4%. The premium has moderated from around 4% earlier, pointing to a potentially limited gain over the issue price at the time of listing.As the NSE listing approaches, investors will be watching movements in the grey market premium, the broader market mood and participation from institutional investors. These factors will be closely followed as the exchange prepares for its debut on the BSE.The Rs 22,562 crore public issue consists entirely of an offer for sale (OFS). A total of 12.64 crore shares are being offered by existing shareholders. As NSE itself is not selling any shares in the issue, the exchange will not receive money raised through the IPO. The proceeds will instead go to the shareholders participating in the OFS.NSE had set the price band for the issue at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share and fixed the lot size at eight shares. At the current grey market premium of 2.4%, the implied listing price works out to around Rs 1,828 per share, compared with the upper end of the IPO price band at Rs 1,785.Subscription to the IPO began on September 17 and ended on September 21, with the issue drawing strong interest from investors across categories. Overall, the IPO was subscribed 5.71 times. The retail investor portion received 1.39 times subscription, while the non-institutional investor (NII) segment was subscribed 6.55 times. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) put in the strongest demand, with their portion receiving 12.68 times subscription.Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Ltd., Morgan Stanley India Company Pvt. Ltd. and HSBC Securities & Capital Markets (India) Pvt. Ltd. have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the issue. Link Intime India Pvt. Ltd. is serving as the registrar.The grey market premium (GMP) for the NSE IPO is currently around Rs 43 per share, equivalent to 2.4%, according to an ET report. This is lower than the roughly 4% premium seen earlier.The current premium is calculated against the upper end of the IPO price band, which is Rs 1,785 per share.The National Stock Exchange is India's largest stock exchange and operates an integrated platform covering trading, clearing, listing, data services and index licensing. Its offerings include the cash market, futures and options, mutual funds, commodity derivatives, currency derivatives, the wholesale debt market and interest rate futures.NSE has remained India's leading exchange by cash market turnover as well as equity derivatives turnover from FY01 through FY26. As of June 2026, the exchange had 132.4 million unique registered investors and 1,328 trading members. It had 3,005 listed entities, with the market capitalization of these entities at around Rs 474.1 trillion.
Article Summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is set to debut on the stock market on September 24, 2026. The shares are scheduled to begin trading on the BSE. With the listing now just a day away, the grey market is indicating a premium of about 2.4%.

Article Title: Gurugram collapses in rains while Greater Noida planned for 30-40 years: Supreme Court
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court

Supreme Court raises infrastructure concerns

What is the Premium FAR scheme?

Government says Premium FAR cannot regularise illegal buildings

Karnataka authorities get four weeks to respond

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said the urban system in Gurugram collapses during rains because adequate investment was not made in infrastructure such as drainage and sewage systems. The court contrasted this with Greater Noida, saying the latter was planned with the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came while the top court was hearing a plea challenging the Karnataka High Court's decision upholding the state's Premium Floor Area Ratio (FAR) scheme.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued notice on the plea filed by the Citizens Action Forum.The bench, however, clarified that the additional FAR available under the scheme should not be used to regularise illegal construction.Chief Justice Surya Kant said there was no visible improvement or addition to the basic infrastructure of the township, such as roads, sewer lines and bus flyovers, despite the additional construction capacity."We have seen in Gurugram how this system collapses if any natural calamity comes.Because, without adding to this infrastructure, you are burdening the size of the plot with multiple storeys," the CJI said.He said the situation was different in Greater Noida because the city had been planned keeping the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came amid arguments over whether Bengaluru's existing infrastructure can support additional construction allowed under the Premium FAR scheme.The Premium FAR scheme allows property owners to purchase additional construction rights beyond the ordinarily permissible FAR by paying prescribed premium charges. The stated objective is to facilitate vertical development and generate revenue for urban local bodies.FAR refers to the ratio of a building's total floor area to the size of the plot on which it stands.Senior advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for the Citizens Action Forum, argued that road width had effectively become the main criterion for granting Premium FAR, despite existing pressure on Bengaluru's parking, water, electricity and other infrastructure.Justice Bagchi also referred to Bengaluru's traffic problems, saying the city has a "traffic nightmare" and that this was a serious concern raised by the petitioner.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state authorities, said the overall additional FAR remained capped at 0.6. He also said existing setback and parking requirements continued to apply and that developers could not simply purchase additional FAR without meeting parking and other regulatory requirements.Mehta said the money collected under the scheme would go into a dedicated fund for civic infrastructure.A key issue before the bench was whether the Premium FAR scheme could be used to regularise unauthorised construction.Sondhi questioned how the new scheme differed from the earlier Akrama-Sakrama scheme, under which unauthorised constructions were legalised. He told the court that a provision in the Greater Bengaluru Authority Act allowed Premium FAR to be used for regularising existing illegal constructions.Mehta rejected the contention and gave an assurance that unauthorised construction covered by the Akrama-Sakrama scheme would not be regularised under the Premium FAR scheme."It has nothing to do with that. Kindly record my statement. It is completely different. You can also pass directions to this effect," Mehta said.He argued that urban space was limited and vertical growth was the way forward, adding that cities were increasingly moving towards vertical development.The Supreme Court asked the Bengaluru authorities to file their response to the plea within four weeks.The case challenges the Karnataka High Court's June 15 judgment upholding the constitutional validity of the Premium FAR scheme. The high court had dismissed petitions arguing that the scheme violated property rights and reduced the value of Transferable Development Rights (TDRs).The Premium FAR scheme was introduced under Section 18-B of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. The high court had held that it did not violate Articles 14, 21 or 300A of the Constitution.The NGO had argued that Premium FAR allowed developers to purchase additional building rights at rates significantly below the market cost of TDRs, thereby undermining TDRs secured by landowners as compensation for land.The high court rejected the argument, holding that a state policy resulting in fluctuations in property values would not by itself make the policy violative of Article 300A.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says urban system in Gurugram collapses during rains because adequate investment was not made in infrastructure. Court contrasted this with Greater Noida, saying the latter was planned with the next 30-40 years in mind. Chief Justice Surya Kant said there was no visible improvement or addition to the basic infrastructure of the township.

Article Title: National film awards will now be at tourist destinations: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Article Text:
President Droupadi Murmu presents the Best Actress in a Leading Role award to Yami Gautam for her performance in Article 370 during the 72nd National Film Awards, in Gujarat, Tuesday

NEW DELHI: On a day Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Kevadia - where ' Statue of Unity ' holds centrestage - became the space for at the 72nd National Film Awards, information and broadcasting minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday said govt plans to take these awards to some of the best tourism destinations across states in the future.He urged all states to send in their proposals of best tourist destinations, and prepare and execute 360 degree development plans in those areas. "The proposal of whichever state is selected, the next national film awards will be held at that tourist destination," he said.Reflecting on PM Narendra Modi's vision when G20 summit was organised in India in 2023, Vaishnaw said that at that time too programmes related to the summit were held across different states. The same is being done with the film awards and, therefore, these are being organised and will be taken to different tourist destinations in the future, he said.
Article Summary: Information and broadcasting minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said govt plans to take these awards to some of the best tourism destinations across states in the future. He urged all states to send in their proposals of best tourist destinations, and prepare and execute 360 degree development plans in those areas.

Article Title: India teams up with EU, Canada & others to defend multilateralism; EAM says rules must be scrupulously followed
Article Text:
S Jaishankar At P4M Summit

India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity, while expressing concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.The declaration followed the announcement of a new initiative titled Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) on the margins of the UN General Assembly that aims to make multilateral bodies more “representative, effective, legitimate and trusted” through middle-power cooperation, amid growing fragmentation and violations of international law.Drawing attention to geopolitical tensions, conflicts and extreme competition, foreign minister S Jaishankar said multilateralism will be best served when international law, rules, and norms are scrupulously observed.Other declaration co-sponsors included Brazil, Barbados and Kenya, making P4M a diverse group of countries that bridges – unlike the G7 and BRICS - the gap between the West and Global South. After the co-sponsors, 16 other countries signed off on the declaration that flagged increasing use of economic interdependence as a source of leverage, disrupting trade, supply chains, investment and development finance in messages directed at both US and China.The declaration stressed reform of multilateral institutions, including the UN, to promote fair trade, prevent conflicts and protect rule of law, while backing fair, open, resilient, predictable and inclusive economic cooperation, including more diversified and resilient global supply chains.The declaration said that the multilateral system founded on the UN Charter remained indispensable, as it had helped provide a framework for peace, decolonisation, prosperity, and human dignity. However, the declaration also said that it must now respond to a world that is more interconnected and complex, more contested and more multipolar.“We affirm the need to uphold and enforce the rules, principles and commitments that remain essential to international order, while renewing and reforming the multilateral system so that it is more effective, representative, inclusive and fit for purpose,” said the declaration, while stressing the joint commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and prohibition of the threat or use of force.The inaugural meeting was co-hosted by European Council President Antonio Costa who said that the P4M will serve as a global network for dialogue, coalition-building and practical cooperation, helping us coordinate our response to shared challenges, with the UN at its core.As he underlined the need for multilateralism to assert itself strongly in these times, Jaishankar also pointed to the issue of terrorism. “The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance ,of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chain, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics, all depend on a will to cooperate,” he said.The minister also flagged the 4F crises of fuel, food, fertilizer and finance cannot be left to itself, saying where new capabilities and concerns arise, there is a very powerful case for frameworks and guardrails.“Where there is a threat of chokepoints dominance and disruption, de-risking and diversifying must be encouraged. And where there is a compelling cause or a powerful case, the like-minded must have the confidence to come together,” said Jaishankar, stressing the need for reformed multilateralism.
Article Summary: India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co- sponsoring a declaration. The declaration expressed a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity. It expressed concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.

Article Title: Exorbitant pricing of drugs is ‘extortion': Supreme Court
Article Text:
If this is not extortion, then what is it, says SC on allowing retailers to overprice drugs

Bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Expressing shock over patients and their families being fleeced by pharma companies and retail medicine sellers, Supreme Court on Tuesday said the exorbitant prices charged was nothing but “dacoity” in broad daylight and questioned the govt’s silence on the pressing issue faced by citizens.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said price fixation of medicines was very important as people were being forced to sell their assets and ornaments to purchase medicines and suggested that all medicines should be brought under the purview of the price control mechanism and be made available under govt-sponsored Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Referring to a cancer drug without naming it, the bench said the pharma company supplied it to retailers at Rs 2,770 but it was sold to patients at an MRP of Rs 27,000.“There are medicines, essential medicines for cancer, which the MRP is 27,000 and the PTR (price to retailer) is Rs 2,700. That’s absolute rampage, carnage, broad daylight dacoity. How can a patient be cheated for a medicine, which the manufacturer sells to the retailer at Rs 2,700 and the MRP is printed at Rs 27,000? It is ten times. It is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take a decision on this are absolutely silent.We don’t need to spell out the reason for that,” the bench said.Additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the govt was not taking an adversarial approach in the matter and it would remain the govt’s endeavour to make medicines available to all. But the bench interrupted him and pointed out that the issue was not about availability but about making them available at a reasonable price.“If that is not extortion, then what is it? People sell their houses, sell their ornaments for getting medicines... Price fixation is very important and all medicines should be brought under price fixation policy. If all medicines are important, then why keep some medicines out of it?” the bench asked. The court was hearing PILs filed by SC advocate K C Jain and Agra-based doctor Sanjay Kulshresthra seeking the court’s intervention on price fixation of medicines.The petitioners placed before the court bills to demonstrate how drugs were being overpriced by pharma companies or by printing a much higher MRP than their actual retail price in the open market, which allowed retailers to sell the medicines at 10-16 times their actual cost.Giving an example, Kulshresthra told the court that the MRP of an antibiotic named Tigebex 50 mg was Rs 5,635 and was sold at that price in corporate hospitals but the same was being sold in the open market at just Rs 350.“In other words, the hospital is charging 16 times its actual retail cost in the market,” he said.The bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing and said, “Why this disparity at all? A medicine which is, as a matter of fact, sold by the manufacturer to the retailer at 10% of its MRP, why has it got this high MRP? Why should there be such disparity? It is a clear cut case of fraud on the face of it.”Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for pharma companies, said they were not the ones making money out of it and sought time to place data before the court, which was allowed.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said price fixation of medicines was very important. They suggested that all medicines should be brought under the purview of the price control mechanism and be made available under govt-sponsored Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing.

Article Title: Prominent citizens oppose AIMPLB's Shariat campaign
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: More than 90 citizens, who identify themselves as progressive Muslim activists, intellectuals and women's rights advocates, have strongly opposed what they cited as the "ill-conceived" nationwide 'Save India, Save Shariat' campaign launched by All India Muslim Personal Law Board ( AIMPLB ) last week.In a statement, they have called upon all progressive forces, civil society organisations and secular political parties to intervene actively to ensure that the demand for a gender-just, religion-neutral Uniform Civil Code is rooted in equality and human rights, rather than being weaponised for communal division.The statement's signatories include Naseeruddin Shah, Zeenat Shaukat Ali, Sultan Shaheen, Teesta Setalvad, Ram Puniyani, Tushar Gandhi, Amol Palekar, Mallika Sarabhai. Ratna Pathak, Javed Anand and Feroze Mithiborwala (Indian Muslims for Secular Democracy-IMSD), Zakia Soman and Noorjahan Safia Niaz (Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan-BMMA), Shamsuddin Tamboli (Muslim Satyashodhak Mandal) and Bader Saeed (Roshni). "The so-called 'God-given Shariat Law' in India are man-made personal laws shaped by patriarchal interpretations and defended by AIMPLB," the statement said, adding that AIMPLB selectively invokes Articles 25-30 (religious freedom), ignoring these rights are subject to public order, morality, and health.
Article Summary: More than 90 citizens, who identify themselves as progressive Muslim activists, intellectuals and women's rights advocates, have strongly opposed the 'Save India, Save Shariat' campaign. They have called upon all progressive forces, civil society organisations and secular political parties to intervene actively to ensure that the demand for a gender-just, religion-neutral Uniform Civil Code is rooted in equality.

Article Title: ED searches office of senior Punjab official over building scam
Article Text:
Enforcement Directorate (ED)

NEW DELHI: In a crackdown on a nexus of senior officials of Punjab govt and builders relating to Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (Gmada), ED Tuesday searched multiple premises in Delhi, Ludhiana, Panchkula, Mohali and Chandigarh, including the office of Gmada and that of IAS officer and principal secretary (housing and urban development) Vikas Garg.It is probing senior officials of Punjab govt and several builders and developers in connection with alleged corruption in Gmada and for the award of projects to builders through auction, waiver of external development charges, interest charges, etc.Searches were conducted on 26 premises “related to Tirupati Infraprojects Pvt Ltd and its promoters, directors and associated persons, besides others”. The other builders under probe include Remigate Buildestates (India) Pvt Ltd, MB Infrabuild Pvt Ltd, Mera Baba Reality Associates Pvt Ltd and Mera Baba Infrastructure Pvt Ltd.“Simultaneously, searches are being conducted at the offices of Gmada and of the department of housing and urban development, Punjab, to gather evidence from the accused entities,” sources said. “Tirupati Infraprojects is also an accused in CBI and ED cases, being allegedly involved in a bank fraud to the tune of Rs 290 crore concerning a project, Radisson Blu hotel, at Paschim Vihar, New Delhi.”“Investigation has revealed that the promoters of Tirupati Infraprojects also control entities Remigate Buildestates (India), MB Infrabuild, which had acquired two prime auction sites at Mohali from Gmada and thereafter obtained substantial financial relief in respect of the dues payable to the authority,” an official said.ED has estimated suspected undue gain to the firms and the loss to the exchequer at more than Rs 100 crore. ED is also searching a consultancy firm, Tila Consultants & Contractors, which deals with various consultancy works of Gmada and is suspected to have acted as an intermediary in the scam.
Article Summary: ED searches premises in Delhi, Ludhiana, Panchkula, Mohali and Chandigarh. It is probing senior officials of Punjab govt and several builders and developers in connection with alleged corruption in Gmada. ED has estimated suspected undue gain to the firms and the loss to the exchequer at more than Rs 100 crore.

Article Title: PM Modi to chair meet to chart govt's next set of priorities
Article Text:
PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Union council of ministers will meet at a Chintan Shivir Wednesday and Thursday to chart govt's "next set of ideas, reforms and priorities" focused on Viksit Bharat@2047 and review progress of key programmes. PM Narendra Modi will chair the two-day brainstorming session.Ahead of the session at Seva Teerth (PMO), Modi directed ministries to prepare plans to engage senior citizens in "mentorship programmes and initiatives of govt", keeping in view India's changing demographic profile. TOI has learnt that social justice ministry has been tasked with this initiative conceptualised by the PMO.Departments have been advised to transformViksit Bharat from a govt initiative into a mass movement as was done during "freedom struggle by Gandhi ji" and to build a youth movement around it through programmes in universities and colleges.Chintan Shivir will see presentations by ministers, including Hardeep Singh Puri and Piyush Goyal, on four major themes including effective communication and implementation of govt programmes. Each group comprising 16-17 ministers held preparatory meetings Monday and Tuesday. PM recently also held discussions with ministers of states.An assessment of cabinet ministers on their social media presence was shared with them. So far, there have been eight presentations and discussions before the council of ministers "It brings together the work done by groups of secretaries, ministries and departments, cabinet secretariat and Niti Aayog including reforms, ease of living, reduction of compliances and other governance priorities," said an official.

Article Title: War on drugs will be at district level: Amit Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday said India’s war on drugs will now be waged at the district level, establishing the local administrative unit as the primary battlefield to dismantle illicit networks.Inaugurating the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and UTs in Delhi, Shah outlined the district-centric strategy, giving an operational break-up for targeting trafficking operations with a ground-up approach. “Under the new framework, districts nationwide will be categorised into three distinct clusters based on their role in the narcotics supply chain — drug manufacturing or entry points, transportation corridors, and high-consumption districts,” Shah said.Correspondingly, enforcement agencies will execute a simultaneous, three-level attack against drug cartels, identifying their primary touchpoints, inter-state distribution systems and local sales networks operating within individual districts. State police forces have been instructed to integrate the conversion of raw information into actionable intelligence directly into their daily organisational culture.To ensure tangible results, Shah mandated an immediate shift across all state ANTFs, seeking a transition from routine meetings to active missions, from simple reporting to proven results, from a seizure-centric mindset to total network dismantling and from initial case registration to final court conviction.Reiterating India’s resolute stance to not allow a single gram of drugs to enter or exit the country, Shah expressed confidence that this synchronised grassroots strategy will secure complete victory and achieve a ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’ by 2029.Shah also directed police departments to abandon surface-level drug seizures in favour of comprehensive backward and forward investigations, financial auditing and tracing of digital links to choke cartel funding. He emphasised the aggressive application of PIT-NDPS Act alongside tight coordination with public prosecutors from investigation to conviction.On emerging global threats, Shah called for specialised ‘out-of-the-box’ officer teams in every state to tackle synthetic drugs, precursor chemical diversion, dark-net markets, crypto transactions and dead-drop delivery systems. Furthermore, he mandated a dedicated campaign to deport and blacklist foreign drug offenders operating in India, while tracking and extraditing overseas fugitives supplying drugs into the country.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday said India’s war on drugs will now be waged at the district level. Shah outlined the district-centric strategy at the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and UTs in Delhi.

Article Title: UPI MDR will fund innovation, protect small merchants: NPCI’s Dilip Asbe
Article Text:
The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed.

Why this sudden move to charge MDR on UPI, and how did you decide on the Rs 2,000 threshold and the 0.4% MDR? Will you review the scheme periodically?

How much is expected to be collected in the first year, around Rs 15,000 crore?

What is the rationale for the charge given that the government can easily foot a bill of Rs 20,000 crore, as it is a tiny fraction of its budget, especially when it spends thousands of crores on non-merit subsidies? Why can't banks, NPCI or RBI bear the burden?

What is being done to ensure that customers are not burdened with MDR? Also, is NPCI proposing a relook at GST?

How do you propose to utilise the money to develop the market? Do you see banks and other service providers offering loyalty points for UPI transactions, as is the case with credit cards?

Will there be a check on merchants and consumers splitting transactions to avoid MDR over Rs 2,000?

The new system has created confusion around several aspects of the scheme...

How do you respond to allegations that the decision was taken under US pressure?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why is the P2PM limit so low?

The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. In an interview with TOI, Dilip Asbe, MD & CEO, explains how the new fee structure protects small transactions while charging larger merchants, who already pay fees on card payments. Besides, there are a host of exemptions aimed at shielding consumers and small merchants. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants, while periodic reviews will assess the model.UPI P2M was charged from inception, and we followed the global model of keeping P2P free and P2M at reasonable cost recovery, much lower than the prescribed MDR for debit and credit cards, net banking or wallets. The government's decision on zero MDR in 2020 helped UPI expand rapidly among merchants during the Covid period. In the last four years, the UPI ecosystem — namely NPCI, banks, fintech start-ups and industry bodies such as the Payments Council of India and IBA — has been seeking a review to ensure a self-sustainable system that can create long-term value for the country, citizens and merchants. UPI growth has slowed, and India remains under-penetrated compared with China and Brazil, where almost 90% of the adult population uses digital payments every day, versus 40% in our case.So, we need investment to expand digital payments, especially among the poor.The charges were finalised primarily keeping in mind the costs incurred by various players to process UPI transactions. Instead of a fixed-fee model, which would penalise low-ticket transactions, we opted for percentage-based charges so that high-ticket transactions with margins can contribute the majority of the MDR. Certain categories with high ticket sizes but lower margins were kept at a flat Rs 5 irrespective of the ticket size, to continue driving adoption. If you review the rates, they are almost at par with global rates for QR-based payments, which are charged similarly without making any exceptions, while these charges remain much lower than those for debit or credit card transactions currently paid by large merchants.It may take some time for the system to settle down. Maybe, in the first year, we will collect Rs 13,000-15,000 crore, of which 5% will be allocated to the small merchant fund to incentivise digital-payment growth among small merchants. We will soon release the guidelines on this.The idea is not to burden small players, as we expect over 80% of the MDR charges to come from businesses with over Rs 1,000 crore turnover. Most of them are already accepting cards and paying much higher MDR on cards under the current construct. There are competing demands on public funds, and this is the best way to make the ecosystem sustainable, grow and innovate without depending on subsidies.NPCI is a not-for-profit entity; all its profits are reinvested in creating infrastructure, reserves for settlement guarantees, innovation and resilience. NPCI needs to not only survive but thrive for the next 100 years.Banks continue to make substantial investments in maintaining and scaling the UPI ecosystem, with annual expenditure often exceeding Rs 2,000 crore for most large banks. At the same time, a Rs 5,000 cash withdrawal can often be substituted by 50 to 100 UPI transactions, highlighting the scale and efficiency of digital payments. While the transition from cash to digital payments has undoubtedly delivered savings through lower cash-handling and ATM-servicing costs, banks also incur significant costs in building and operating resilient, secure and scalable UPI payment infrastructure.Over the last six years, the overall ecosystem has invested over Rs 75,000 crore to maintain and grow the UPI ecosystem without much cost recovery. These investments and innovations will benefit the country in the long run.Running the UPI ecosystem requires around Rs 21,000 crore annually, and we have sought to protect small merchants and low-value payments to help smaller firms raise capital and invest. The idea is also to have more players to increase competition. As a result, person-to-person transactions and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000, with no upper cap on cumulative or repeat transactions, all recurring payments or AutoPay, and small individual merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month into their own accounts will not face any MDR. Since most of the MDR will be generated from merchants who already accept card payments, the consumer price is already factored into MDR charges, or else we would have seen merchants offering major discounts for UPI and RuPay debit card transactions over the last six years. We have prohibited platform fees and merchants charging customers. We plan to review it periodically along with the ecosystem. On GST, I have no comments to offer since this decision will be made by the finance ministry and GST Council. However, major large merchants will claim an input tax credit for the GST paid.The objective of these charges is to ensure the ecosystem thrives, becomes self-sustainable, and is able to innovate and create value that, in turn, grows UPI. Today, we observe that payment methods with good cost recovery tend to have better innovation and features. For example, EMIs, rewards and discount offers help grow merchant sales, particularly in categories such as electronics. Once cost recovery starts, the ecosystem will create a major drive to onboard new consumers and merchants, install more sound boxes and increase activity in under-penetrated geographies and categories through digitalisation. Amid evolving times and landscapes, it will also allow the ecosystem to invest proactively in cybersecurity and resilience.Any policy that has a ceiling or a floor has these second-order effects. If the consumer is ready to participate in splitting the transactions based on a merchant's request, we do not foresee any harm in this and, accordingly, no upper cap on such transactions has been defined. We believe this may, at best, be a short-term phenomenon and that consumer experience will ultimately win in the long run. What we have seen globally and in India is that it is primarily the consumer's choice that drives digital payments.Yes, but we are working with industry bodies and ecosystem participants to provide clarity. For example, some people have interpreted the no-MDR limit below Rs 2,000 as a daily cap and not a per-transaction limit, which is not the case.The USTR has a reference to a UPI market-share cap of 30%, as well as NCMC standards access to other competing international schemes, which is a fair and factual point, and we believe it must be a country's prerogative to make that decision. We didn't find any reference to charges or MDR, and, as I said above, it benefits competing companies to keep it free.This is more like an intermediate step for a merchant moving from receiving money via standard P2P to graduating into a proper P2M merchant so that it gets the support of a sound box, POS machine or other ancillary services. Even when P2PM merchants move to a proper merchant, they continue to receive transactions up to Rs 2,000 without any charges or cap.
Article Summary: The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants.

Article Title: Fortis investors flag legal overhang after Delhi HC order
Article Text:
Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence.

Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court ’s order seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters, Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence.The Aug 31 high court order came in a case arising from Japanese firm Daiichi Sankyo’s efforts to enforce its arbitral award against the erstwhile Fortis promoters. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the order.Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold over half -- 57% shareholding, while the retail share is over 11% in the company.``The question for the market is whether a transaction that has cleared the entire approval architecture — board, shareholders, CCI, SEBI, the Takeover Code, ever becomes settled’’, Shriram Subramanian MD and founder of InGovern, a proxy advisory firm, told TOI.In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore.``Questioning a transaction long cleared by all regulators and seeking its forensic audit after nearly a decade, will open a can of worms’’, he added.IHH is a credible strategic investor, and Fortis, after years of promoter-related turmoil and uncertainty, is now on a more stable footing, investors feel, and prolonged legal proceedings could create uncertainty.While the court has made clear that the forensic audit is a fact-finding exercise and does not, by itself, impose liability, investors said the process could still have wider implications for the company.``Capital is mobile and investors have alternatives; prolonged uncertainty can therefore have consequences for the company and its shareholders’’, InGovern said in a note, shared with TOI.The acquisition was approved by the board, cleared by the CCI, and completed under the SEBI Takeover Regulations through an open offer SEBI itself permitted. Neither IHH nor Fortis was a party to the arbitration, the award or the execution proceedings.Investors are also concerned about the possibility of the company being drawn into the matter at a later stage, including through the doctrine of “reverse veil piercing”.The company has also challenged this in its special leave petition arguing that reverse piercing, under which a company’s assets could potentially be subjected to the personal debts or obligations of its (erstwhile) controlling shareholder, has not been recognised by Indian courts.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court’s order seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters, Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the order. In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has prepared 81 artificial ponds for people to immerse Ganesh idols at designated sites instead of the Yamuna or other water bodies.The government has also set up 110 collection centres for dignified disposal of old and damaged idols and religious material.The two measures form part of an initiative aimed at balancing religious practices with cleanliness and environmental protection.The initiative will provide designated collection containers at suitable locations, including temples, where devotees can deposit old, damaged idols and other puja material instead of leaving them in public places, chief minister Rekha Gupta said.She said such material is often left under trees, in parks, along roadsides and at other public places due to religious sentiments, creating challenges for cleanliness and the environment.Preparations have also been completed at 81 locations across Delhi for artificial immersion ponds for Ganesh idols. The arrangements cover all 13 revenue districts and include security, sanitation, lighting, medical assistance, emergency response and traffic management, according to a statement.The chief minister has appealed to devotees to immerse Ganesh idols only at designated artificial immersion sites and not in the Yamuna or other water bodies.She also urged people not to dispose of puja material, flowers, garlands and other religious items in rivers or water bodies and to give preference to eco-friendly idols.The government has advised devotees to avoid idols made of Plaster of Paris, colours containing harmful chemicals and decorative materials that can damage water bodies and the environment.Arrangements have also been made for removal of idol remains and other material from immersion sites after the festivities, followed by cleaning of the locations as per the prescribed process, it said.The initiative is aimed at providing organised and clean spaces for people to follow their religious traditions while reducing pressure on public spaces and water bodies, the statement said.Gupta said religious faith and environmental protection should complement each other and urged Delhi residents to use only designated collection centres for damaged idols and religious material and artificial immersion sites for Ganesh idols.She said maintaining a clean Delhi was a shared responsibility of the government and citizens, and called for public participation to balance faith, cleanliness and environmental protection.The Ganesh festival began on September 14 and will conclude on September 25, when a large number of idols will be immersed after colourful processions.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the steep markup on essential cancer medicines, with the bench describing the practice as “broad daylight dacoity” against patients. The remarks came after the court was informed that an essential cancer drug had a maximum retail price (MRP) of Rs 27,000, even though its price to retailers (PTR) was Rs 2,700, a tenfold difference.“There are essential medicines for cancer on which the MRP is printed as Rs 27,000 while the PTR is Rs 2,700. This is absolute rampage and carnage. This is broad daylight dacoity with patients,” news agency PTI quoted a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta saying.“It is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take action on this are silent,” it saidThe bench said the price gap was “absolutely shocking” and questioned how such pricing could be allowed.“The MRP is 10 times the rate at which it is provided to the retailers. If this is not extortion, then what it is? People sell their houses, ornaments to get treatment,” the bench said.The observations were made while the court was hearing two petitions dealing with drug-related issues, including demands for tighter price controls.One of the petitioners also raised the issue of registered medical practitioners prescribing generic medicines, and stressed the need for greater regulation of medicine prices.Additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the Centre in one of the cases, told the court that the government was not approaching the litigation as an adversarial matter.The bench said fixing medicine prices remained a major concern and adjourned the matter to September 29.One of the petitions seeks measures to make drug formulations more affordable by preventing alleged unethical pricing of essential medicines by pharmaceutical companies and retailers. It also seeks strict enforcement of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, to check violations of price-control rules and disproportionate retailer margins.The other petition seeks disciplinary action against doctors for not prescribing generic medicines to patients.
Article Summary: Supreme Court raises concerns over steep pricing of essential cancer medicines. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the price gap was ‘absolutely shocking’ The bench said fixing medicine prices remained a major concern and adjourned the matter to September 29.

Article Title: ‘Weighing pros & cons of allowing airport operators to run airline: Naidu'
Article Text:

No fare caps this festive season:

NEW DELHI: Govt is weighing the pros and cons of allowing Adani Group, which operates Mumbai airport, to run an airline. The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their “operation, management and development agreement” (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently the Adani Group had sought amendment to the same.“Govt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand. Our ambition is to have at least five airlines with at least 100 aircraft each. So if someone wants to start an airline, govt supports the idea. The issue is an airport (Mumbai and Delhi) doing so. We are examining the pros and cons of the same,” Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said here Tuesday.Naidu said no decision on the Adani request has been taken so far. “We need to create a system where the cons (of allowing such a move) are taken care of. Pros we know. As such in govt there is no clause or rule anywhere which stops airport operators from having airlines other than the OMDA agreement for Delhi and Mumbai. If let us say BIAL (Bengaluru operator), which is still a private operator, wants to operate an airline, there is no rule stopping him.That’s why we have to take a balanced approach,” said Naidu.Adani’s request has divided the airline industry with IndiGo promoter Rahul Bhatia opposing the move and Akasa founder Vinay Dube being in favour of the same.The minister spoke about other issues at an UDAN event here Tuesday. “The aviation ministry, Airports Authority of India and 21 States & UTs (have) come together and sign MoUs to put a greater focus on speed, sustainability and long-term viability of projects in the next phase of UDAN… 100 airports will be developed under challenge mode over the next 10 years,” Naidu said.The cash-strapped airline’s woes have been mounting and its passengers often suffer delays running in several hours. “We are closely monitoring SpiceJet’s operations and finances through the aviation ⁠regulatory body to ensure safety is not compromised. Operational and financial scrutiny is being done. SpiceJet got Rs 150 crore under ECLGS. Getting more funds is something the airline has to work with banks with. It is a private airline. Our priority is to ensure passengers don’t face inconvenience and that safety is not compromised,” Naidu said.“The intention of the ministry is that all pilots must get tested within a year. The framework for the same has to be issued by the regulator DGCA. We have given our intent to them and they are holding deliberation with stakeholders. The DGCA rule change to ensure this is expected,” said the minister.Airfares will not be capped this festive season and the aviation ministry will advise airlines to keep the same at reasonable levels, said the minister. The hike being seen in recent dues is not due to the spike in demand but due to increased jet fuel prices.“We engage with airlines continuously and have regular meetings with them. And we definitely point it out to them that during this festive season, you have to ensure that the fair prices are kept at a reasonable level so that the people who want to travel, especially in these important times, get to see the benefit,” the minister said.
Article Summary: The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their “operation, management and development agreement’ (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently the Adani Group had sought amendment to the same. “Govt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand,” said the minister.

Article Title: IGIA immigration lapse: ‘Entire hub, spoke ecosystem strengthened now,’ says Naidu

NEW DELHI: Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Tuesday said authorities have learnt from the recent immigration lapse at Delhi Airport where three hub and spoke passengers of Air India flew from Amritsar to Germany via Delhi without clearing immigration and taking corrective steps to ensure such an incident never recurs. Reiterating India’s goal to become a global aviation hub, the minister said hub and spoke will be expanded to more airports while plugging all gaps to create a foolproof seamless system.“There should be no compromise with security detail in our airport operations. We want convenient and seamless international transfers. That is where hub and spoke comes in. India truly believes in becoming a global hub. So far three airports have hub and spoke and we will expand this list. There was a lapse. The aviation ministry responded and issued a show cause to AI so that any security related issue should be addressed,” Naidu said.Authorities met AI officials and “understood the checks and balances that have been put in place. Now there are multiple parameters in place to ensure this does not recut. Things have settled down. We have created a robust ecosystem. This lapse has been an understanding for us,” he added.The feedback to the hub and spoke with passengers clearing customs and immigration at the local spoke airport has been “great”. “This has led to convenience to passengers, especially for women traveling with children and connecting domestic to international at Delhi late at night,” the minister said.The Union aviation ministry had issued a show cause notice to Air India for lapses that saw three foreigners fly into Delhi from Amritsar on Sept 4 and then within an hour depart for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight without the mandatory immigration check. “Air India personnel who were to escort passengers through respective pathways were found to be at fault and they were immediately suspended. Have created multiple systems now; the role digi yatra role plays; how passengers move at connecting airports. The ecosystem has been strengthened,” Naidu said.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Election Commission to file its response over the basis on which persons are being issued notices under the "logical discrepancies" category during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Delhi.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya bagchi and Justice V Mohana specifically questioned the manner in which the poll panel was generating and communicating the notices.Justice Bagchi asked EC to examine whether notices were being issued mechanically and whether voters were being adequately informed about the reason for the notice. The poll panel also informed the top court that the 12 documents referred to in the verification process were not exhaustive.As per the petitioners, the draft electoral roll in Delhi excluded around 47 lakh names, while notices were issued to around 33 lakh other voters whose names remained in the draft roll.

Article Title: India sees rise in both overweight and underweight
Article Text:
AI generated image for representational purpose

The dual problem

Trend reversal in low BMI

Trend reversal

How states fared

State-wise comparison for men

State-wise comparison for women

Urban-rural divide

Contrasting trend in urban and rural areas

India not following global pattern?

The district-level analysis

A normal BMI can hide muscle loss and excess fat

Blood sugar also climbed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sedentary lifestyles are often blamed for rising obesity. It is perhaps the most obvious explanation, repeated ad nauseam in this digital age, where often the entire world stays within our six-inch screen. But data from the government's latest pan-India health survey (NFHS-6) suggest something quieter, and potentially more complicated for policymakers. Below-normal BMI has stopped retreating in India even as overweight and obesity rise.The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is the government's main source of data on health and nutrition, run by the International Institute for Population Sciences for the Union health ministry. Its sixth round, NFHS-6, covered about 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts, with fieldwork running from May 2023 to December 2024. It reports 101 indicators for India and every state and union territory except Manipur.Among women aged 15-49, the share with below-normal BMI rose marginally from 18.7% in NFHS-5 to 19.7% in NFHS-6, while the share classified as overweight or obese rose steeply from 24% to 30.7%.Hence the calculated share of women in the normal-BMI range fell from 57.3% to 49.6%, a decline of 7.7 percentage points.Men aged 15-49 are moving in the same direction. Below-normal BMI rose from 16.2% to 19.7%, while overweight or obesity increased from 22.9% to 27.3%. Hence the share of men in the normal-BMI range shrank from 60.9% to 53%, a decline of 7.9 percentage points.BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. For these indicators, NFHS classifies BMI below 18.5 as below normal and BMI of 25 or above as overweight or obese. It does not publish the normal range in between; TOI calculated that middle by subtracting the two published shares from 100.The NFHS-6 fact sheets are provisional, and without unit-level data it has not been tested whether the changes are statistically significant.Comparable figures for both sexes begin with NFHS-3, and below-normal BMI fell in each round until now. Among women it went from 35.6% in NFHS-3 (2005-06) to 22.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) and 18.7% in NFHS-5; among men, from 34.2% to 20.2% and then 16.2%.NFHS-6 is the first of these rounds in which the below-normal share rises for both sexes, and men's share, lower than women's in each earlier round, now matches it at 19.7%. Overweight has risen in every round, from 12.6% to 30.7% among women since NFHS-3 and from 9.3% to 27.3% among men.Below-normal BMI increased from NFHS-5 in 20 of the 35 state/UT comparisons among women and 27 of 35 among men. Overweight or obesity rose even more widely, in 33 of 35 among women and 28 of 35 among men. Both rose together in 19 of the comparisons for women and 20 for men.Among women, just seven of the 35 states and Union territories in the NFHS-6 release had a calculated normal-BMI share below 50% in NFHS-5; in NFHS-6, that number has risen to 16. So in 16 states, more than half of women in the 15-49 age group are either overweight or underweight. Among men, only one of the 35 — Puducherry — was below 50% in NFHS-5. In NFHS-6, 11 are below 50%.Rajasthan recorded the sharpest increase in below-normal BMI for both sexes: from 19.6% to 27.3% among women, a rise of 7.7 percentage points, and from 14% to 24.7% among men, up 10.7 points. Other large increases in low BMI among women were in Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand; among men, the sharpest increases were in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Tripura and Delhi.At the other end, Lakshadweep saw the largest increase in overweight or obesity among women, from 33.5% to 50.1%, followed by Sikkim, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Among men, the biggest increase was in Chandigarh, from 34.4% to 48.5%, followed by Goa, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and West Bengal.The state numbers show this is not confined to a few pockets.Among urban women, 13.2% have below-normal BMI and 42.8% are overweight or obese. Among rural women, below-normal BMI is much higher at 22.5%, while overweight or obesity stands at 25.5%. Against NFHS-5, below-normal BMI among rural women has risen from 21.2%, while the urban estimate is unchanged at 13.2%. Overweight or obesity rose in both, from 33.2% to 42.8% in urban areas and from 19.7% to 25.5% in rural areas.Men show a similar urban-rural divide. Among urban men, 14.9% have below-normal BMI and 36.3% are overweight or obese. Among rural men, 21.9% have below-normal BMI and 23% are overweight or obese. Compared with NFHS-5, low BMI among urban men rose from 13% to 14.9%, while among rural men it rose more sharply, from 17.8% to 21.9%. Overweight or obesity increased from 29.8% to 36.3% in urban areas and from 19.3% to 23% in rural areas. Among men, the rise in low BMI was larger in rural India, while the increase in excess weight was sharper in urban India.Dr Sadajit Banerjee, a Kolkata-based internal medicine and geriatrics specialist, says that as an urban doctor he has been seeing mostly a shift towards overweight. Patients increasingly arrive asking about semaglutide and tirzepatide, having read about them; those whose BMI is still within acceptable limits are advised on lifestyle change instead.Most urban Indians, he says, do not seem motivated enough to exercise or change how they live, while others are frightened of the side effects of those drugs. The patients who take up either route readily are usually the ones who already have diabetes or another metabolic disorder. At population level, the coexistence of low BMI and overweight or obesity is consistent with what the World Health Organization calls the double burden of malnutrition. Low BMI is one marker of undernutrition rather than a complete measure of it.Most of the world has been moving in one direction. A 2024 Lancet analysis by the NCD Risk Factor Collaboration, covering 200 countries and territories, found obesity rising almost everywhere between 1990 and 2022 and more than a billion people living with obesity, while adult underweight fell in most countries.That is what makes the NFHS-6 reading unusual: India's overweight share is rising in line with the global pattern, but its below-normal share is not falling. A Global Burden of Disease study put India second only to China, at 180 million adults aged 25 and older with overweight or obesity in 2021. That is a modelled estimate on a different age base.The fact sheets report these BMI measures only for women, so the district picture is a picture of women. The female BMI indicators exclude women who were pregnant or had given birth in the preceding two months.Of the 713 district records in the release, 680 can be compared with NFHS-5, where both BMI figures are available for both rounds. In 372 of those 680, or 54.7%, both ends grew at once: more women with below-normal BMI, and more women overweight or obese. All districts in Punjab, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Delhi and Goa fall below 50% on the calculated female normal-BMI measure. So do the overwhelming majority in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Haryana and Karnataka.BMI can also conceal what it is measuring. With the elderly population growing, Banerjee says he is seeing patients whose BMI is skewed by sarcopenia — too little protein and too little exercise producing muscle loss on one side and fat gain on the other. The number on the chart often stays in the normal range. Such patients may have low muscle mass and excess body fat despite an apparently normal BMI, risks that BMI alone can miss.NFHS-6 also tested blood sugar, on a different age base of 15 and above, against 15-49 for BMI. The share of women with high or very high blood sugar, above 140 mg/dl, or taking medication for diabetes rose from 13.5% to 17.8%; among men, from 15.6% to 20.9%. Urban prevalence is higher on both counts, at 21.9% among women and 23.9% among men, against 16.2% and 19.7% in rural areas.The fact sheets do not establish cause and effect.Overweight and obesity are rising fast, and low BMI has stopped retreating. Across much of the country both are now visible at the same time, which leaves public-health programmes carrying two problems rather than watching one give way to the other. For Banerjee, they are not two problems at all. "Overnourished or undernourished, both fall in the malnourished category," he says. Much of the chatter is about improving urban lifestyles. How rural India gets proper nutrition is the question policymakers will have to answer.
Article Summary: National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is the government's main source of data on health and nutrition. Its sixth round, NFHS-6, covered about 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts, with fieldwork running from May 2023 to December 2024. Below-normal BMI has stopped retreating in India even as overweight and obesity rise.

Article Title: ‘Global order under stress’: Jaishankar calls for stronger multilateralism at UNGA
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar during P4M Summit

External affairs minister S Jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism to navigate rising geopolitical tensions, conflicts and global competition, as he co-chaired the first Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa on Monday (local time). The summit was held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.Minister Jaishankar stressed the need for greater international cooperation and called for steps to address ongoing conflicts, create safeguards for emerging technologies and reduce risks linked to dominance and disruption. He also stressed the importance of international law, rules and norms.In a post on X, Jaishankar said the summit provided an opportunity to underline the importance of multilateralism at a time when international cooperation is facing pressure from intense competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He highlighted the need to address the specific dimensions of ongoing conflicts, establish frameworks and safeguards for emerging capabilities, and reduce risks by diversifying against dominance and disruption. He also underlined the importance of international law, rules and norms.The EAM further called for “reformed multilateralism”, saying more participative discussions and transparent decision-making could help restore hope in the UN system and strengthen countries’ resolve to work together.Addressing the summit, Jaishankar thanked European Council President Antonio Costa for initiating the forum and said India was pleased to join as a co-sponsor. He said the global order was under stress, with a long-running rebalancing of the world taking a different shape amid intensifying competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He said that if these pressures were left unchecked, they could undermine the spirit of international cooperation, making it crucial for multilateralism to assert itself more strongly."We meet at a time when the global order is under stress. For some decades, the world has witnessed a steady rebalancing, which was a long-expected structural evolution. However, extreme competition, geopolitical tensions, and actual conflicts have given this an entirely different character. If left unchecked, it would call into question the very spirit of international cooperation. That is why it is so essential that multilateralism asserts itself strongly at this juncture. "Jaishankar also highlighted the range of issues that he said depended on countries' willingness to cooperate, including peace and international security, climate action and climate justice, emerging technologies, development finance, countering terrorism, strengthening supply chains, disaster resilience and pandemic preparedness."At stake here are very real issues, not just words and expressions. The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance, of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chains, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics. All depend on a will to cooperate."The summit also saw Jaishankar make a case for Reformed Multilateralism, with participative deliberations and transparent decision-making being highlighted as ways to provide hope and optimism to the UN system and reinforce countries' resolve to work together.Meanwhile, Slovakia backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council on Monday, with foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.Blanar's remarks came after Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion". Discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties.Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week in New York and is scheduled to address the General Debate on September 26.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism to navigate rising geopolitical tensions, conflicts and global competition. He co-chaired the first Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa. The summit was held on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.
