Article Title: Govt staff outside CGHS areas can now opt for scheme
Article Text:
Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), even if there is no CGHS Wellness Centre in their city.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), even if there is no CGHS Wellness Centre in their city.The Union health ministry has removed the geographical restriction that earlier prevented eligible employees outside the prescribed CGHS area from opting for the scheme. The move will benefit employees residing or posted outside the prescribed coverage area.Earlier, an employee’s eligibility for CGHS depended on where they lived or were posted. Where a 5-km limit was prescribed, coverage was linked to the area around a CGHS Wellness Centre. Employees outside the prescribed area could not opt for CGHS.Under the new rule, an eligible employee residing or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can opt for the scheme by paying the prescribed CGHS contribution and meeting the other eligibility conditions.However, the choice is a one-time decision and will be final and binding. It will also apply to all eligible dependents of the employee.Employees opting for CGHS cannot simultaneously claim medical benefits under the Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944.Their eligible family members will also have to be covered under the same system.The employee will have to continue paying the prescribed CGHS subscription irrespective of where they subsequently reside or are posted. No travelling or daily allowance will be admissible for treatment or procurement of medicines under CGHS.The new provision does not give employees already residing or posted within a CGHS-covered area the option to shift from CGHS to medical facilities under the CS(MA) Rules.Employees who do not exercise the new option will continue to be governed by the CS(MA) Rules, wherever applicable.The new provisions have come into force with immediate effect. The ministry has issued an option and undertaking form for employees who wish to opt for CGHS.
Article Summary: Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme. The Union health ministry has removed the geographical restriction that earlier prevented eligible employees outside the prescribed CGHS area from opting for the scheme.

Article Title: Hospitals told to report serious medical device events within 15 days
Article Text:
​IPC has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A faulty insulin pump that delivers too much insulin, an infusion pump that gives medicines too quickly, a pulse oximeter showing incorrect oxygen levels or a defibrillator failing during a cardiac emergency will now come under a more systematic hospital safety-monitoring system.The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. Serious adverse events have to be reported to the Materiovigilance Programme of India (MvPI) within 15 days, while non-serious adverse events and certain potentially harmful near-miss incidents have to be reported within 30 days.Patients too have a direct role. Those who notice that a medical device is not functioning properly or experience an adverse event can inform the treating hospital or healthcare professional and directly report suspected device-related events to IPC.IPC has provided a toll-free helpline, 1800-180-3024, for consumers and other stakeholders. It supports reporting in 10 languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.Importantly, the system is not limited to cases in which a patient is actually injured. A device malfunction or quality problem detected before use can be treated as a near miss. If it could potentially cause harm during future use, it is reportable within 30 days even when no patient has been harmed.The guidance also says suspected device-related events should be reported even when it has not yet been established that the device caused the problem, allowing the event to be assessed and investigated further.The guidance, prepared by IPC in collaboration with the World Health Organization India and other stakeholders, covers medical devices including in-vitro diagnostic devices, implants, life-support equipment and newer artificial intelligence-enabled and software-based devices.Hospitals have been asked to actively monitor critical devices, including invasive, implantable and life-supporting equipment. Their performance, malfunctions, complaints and near misses should be reviewed weekly or monthly based on usage and risk, with heightened monitoring of devices under IPC safety alerts or advisories.Each department should have a designated nodal person for monitoring, staff sensitisation and timely reporting. Lists of monitored devices should be displayed in intensive care units, operation theatres, catheterisation laboratories and specialty wards.The guidance was unveiled on Monday by Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel during National Pharmacovigilance Week. The government also announced approval of the Biovigilance Programme of India, under which IPC will lead monitoring of adverse events associated with medicines and biological products used in organ and tissue transplantation.
Article Summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. Serious adverse events have to be reported to the Materiovigilance Programme of India within 15 days. Non-serious adverse events and certain potentially harmful near-miss incidents must be reported within 30 days.

Article Title: 'No burden for consumers': Sitharaman clarifies who will pay MDR on UPI transactions
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), saying that the mechanism will be imposed on operators and will not be passed on to customers. Addressing ongoing speculations around the charges, FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.Speaking to ANI, the finance minister said that she had already addressed the issue in Parliament, stressing that MDR is a charge between payment operators and will not be 'burdened' on UPI users.Sitharaman stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India.”It does not apply to transactions below Rs 2,000. It is neither a tax nor a cess; the funds will not be deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India. It is a charge levied by service providers to improve the system and provide better service, not for small transactions. Moreover, it is a charge between operators; it will not be passed on to the consumer. The burden does not fall on the customer,” she said.Sitharaman said she had given the same clarification earlier too, when the issue came up during the parliamentary session.“I provided a clarification on this very point when the issue was raised during the parliamentary session. Spreading misinformation, fueling debates based on it, and using that narrative to attack the government has become a habit for the opposition. This is wrong; there is an effort to spread misconceptions and mislead the public. The public needs to remain vigilant," Sitharaman added.Meanwhile, Niti Aayog NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri had also backed the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions, saying that businesses should find ways to sustain themselves instead of relying on government subsidies.Lahiri drew on the words of ancient philosopher Chanakya to make his point, saying a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower — “gently, gradually, and without inflicting pain or bruising the petals”.“So you have to find ways of sustaining businesses without having to give subsidy,” Lahiri told reporters on the sidelines of an event.He clarified that the view was his personal opinion and did not represent NITI Aayog’s official position.The government has ruled out any rethink on the decision, with a senior official telling PTI, “There is no question of a re-think.”FM Sitharaman’s clarification comes after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) introduced a new MDR framework on September 15. Under the framework, an MDR of 0.4 per cent will apply to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, subject to a cap of Rs 300 per transaction.Consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI. The government has said that around 96 per cent of P2M transactions will remain unaffected, while the MDR will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) She stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India. FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.

Article Title: Nationwide strike: Banks to remain shut from Monday for three days - what customers need to know
Article Text:
Banks to remain shut for 5 days

What should customers do now?

Here’s what customers could do to avoid disruption:

Complete branch-dependent work beforehand: Customers with requirements that need a branch visit or intervention from bank staff may need to plan them before the proposed strike period.

Customers with requirements that need a branch visit or intervention from bank staff may need to plan them before the proposed strike period. Use mobile banking: Customers can use Mobile Banking for their banking needs.

Why are banks planning a strike?

What has the government said?

Do you have a pending bank visit, payment or other transactions lined up for the month-end? You may want to get it done by Friday!Banking operations across the country are set to face disruption as bank unions have planed a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With the strike following a weekend holiday, customers could face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations take place.With banking services likely to face disruption around the end of September, customers may want to plan their banking requirements in advance. Several public sector banks have already advised customers to use digital channels if the strike goes ahead.Services available through digital channels can continue to be accessed through those channels if the strike materialises. The disruption could also affect businesses, government transactions and international banking operations, apart from causing inconvenience to the public.The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), which claims to represent 90 per cent of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is a concrete and positive development on its main demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” UFBU said in a statement after the meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday remained inconclusive. The union said that in the absence of such a development, it would be constrained to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.The meeting was held a day after the finance ministry appealed to bank employees to refrain from strikes and resolve their remaining demands through dialogue.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS).Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.Representatives of the department of financial services (DFS) and the ministry of finance told the conciliation meeting that the government had been taking several initiatives for the welfare of bank employees. They said five-day banking was also under consideration, but the government would need to take into account the views of various other stakeholders before taking a decision.The representatives therefore asked the UFBU to defer the strike and continue the dialogue.The finance ministry had said that strikes disrupt banking services, inconvenience the public and affect the business of banks. It also said such disruptions ultimately harm the interests of bank employees and that no fruitful outcome is achieved through strikes.The government has assured that it remains committed to the welfare and well-being of bank employees and to addressing their genuine concerns through constructive engagement.
Article Summary: Banking operations across the country are set to face disruption. Bank unions have planed a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With the strike following a weekend holiday, customers could face an effective five-day disruption in banking services. The disruption could also affect businesses, government transactions and international banking operations.

Article Title: Gold prices surge 60% from Rs 98,000 to Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams in a year; Ganesh Chaturthi sales fall 15% as buyers switch to lighter jewellery, also buy coins
Article Text:
Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses.

Gold prices high

Growing interest in coins

Gold hallmarking charges rise

A huge rise in gold prices from the same time last year has led to a drop in gold sales this Ganesh Chaturthi . Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms, with consumers either reducing the quantity they bought or opting for lighter jewellery as a sharp increase in gold prices made purchases more expensive, industry executives said.In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams, including 3% goods and services tax. This was around 60% higher than the Rs 98,000 per 10 grams recorded on Ganesh Chaturthi last year, which fell on August 28.“Domestic gold prices have remained at a historic high, which has impacted volume sales. But overall the mood is optimistic, with many people resorting to old gold jewellery exchanges to buy new jewellery, which is mostly lightweight,” said Surendra Mehta, national secretary, India Bullion & Jewellers Association, according to an ET report.Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses towards the peak wedding season. Since weddings are also taking place during the festive period, retailers expect buyers to increasingly seek jewellery that can serve multiple purposes, from celebrations and gifting to regular wear.“We are seeing greater interest in diamonds as buyers seek jewellery that is versatile enough for celebrations, gifting and everyday wear,” said Rohan Hemdev, director, Ananya Jewels.Kumar Jain, owner of Umedmal Tilokchand Zaveri, a 100-year-old outlet in Mumbai's Zaveri Bazaar, said demand for bullion in the form of coins and bars had picked up during this year's Ganesh Chaturthi, although volumes remained below last year's level.“Bullion sales in the form of coins and bars have shown traction this Ganesh Chaturthi, even though the volume is lesser than last year.”The increased preference for coins and bars suggests that consumers are still setting aside money for gold during auspicious occasions, but the elevated price of jewellery is making them more cautious about their purchases.The trend also reflects the broader conditions in India's gold market. According to the World Gold Council, the festive season began on a cautious note as the sharp rise in gold prices prompted consumers to adopt a wait-and-watch approach and defer discretionary purchases.Wedding-related demand, however, has remained comparatively resilient, while physical investment demand has stayed steady.There is also growing interest among younger consumers in purchasing jewellery for themselves. Women, in particular, are increasingly buying jewellery to celebrate festivals as well as personal milestones.Hemdev expects festive-season sales to register double-digit growth, helped by wedding demand, rising disposable incomes and evolving consumption habits. He also pointed to the growing role of digital platforms, social media, influencers and celebrity collaborations in making jewellery more aspirational and appealing to younger consumers.“With the ongoing festive season, we expect buying interest to gradually pick up, especially as consumers and jewellery retailers prepare for the period,” said Darshan Desai, CEO, Aspect Bullion & Refinery.In the meantime, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles just before the start of the festive season. The charge, which was earlier Rs 45 per gold article, has now been raised to Rs 75. The fee for silver articles, however, remains unchanged at Rs 35.The change was notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.BIS hallmarking is the system used to certify the purity of precious metal articles under the Bureau of Indian Standards framework. A hallmarked article carries three important identifiers: the BIS logo, the karat or millesimal fineness and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers will now be charged Rs 75 for every gold article sent for hallmarking. A minimum charge of Rs 200 will apply to each consignment.There has been no change in the hallmarking fee for silver. Jewellers will continue to pay Rs 35 per silver article to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs), with a minimum consignment charge of Rs 150.
Article Summary: Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms. In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams. The Bureau of Indian Standards has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles just before the start of the festive season.

Article Title: “Every child deserves to be confident”: Patrick Mahomes’ $15,000 literacy move helped put nearly 6,000 books in Kansas City kids’ hands while giving homeless children a fresh start
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes’ $15,000 literacy move helped put nearly 6,000 books in Kansas City kids’ hands (Getty Images)

Patrick Mahomes turned $15,000 into nearly 6,000 books for Kansas City kids

Patrick Mahomes also helped 50 homeless children get a fresh start

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes has found another way to help Kansas City children, and this one starts with a book. On May 31, 2025, his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation announced a $15,000 donation to the Kansas City Public Library’s Summer Reading Program. The money helped the library purchase nearly 6,000 books for local children and support its effort to reduce summer learning loss.The donation added another piece to Mahomes’ literacy work. His foundation had already backed reading programmes across Kansas City, while his #ReadFor15 campaign encourages children to spend at least 15 minutes reading each day.The Kansas City Public Library received the $15,000 award as part of its continuing partnership with the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. The money funded nearly 6,000 books that the library planned to distribute to Kansas City children through its 2025 Summer Reading Program.The foundation also pointed to summer learning loss. It cited studies showing that students in third through fifth grade can lose as much as 20% of their previous reading gains during the summer break.The library had a strong base to build on. Its 2024 Summer Reading Program attracted a record 15,060 registered participants.In 2025, the programme ran from May 30 through August 15. Every person who registered received a free book, while participants could also complete a five-book challenge and earn a reward.Mahomes spoke about the value of reading in the foundation’s May 31 announcement.“Reading every day is so important. It helps us grow, learn, and dream big,” Patrick Mahomes said in the announcement of his foundation’s partnership with the Kansas City Public Library.The donation also followed Mahomes’ March 31 appearance at the Read for 15 Reading Rally at T-Mobile Center. Around 3,000 students attended the Kansas City event, which promoted a 15-minute daily reading habit.“Reading is the foundation for success in school and in life,” Mahomes said at the March 31 Reading Rally. He also encouraged children to build a daily reading habit that could be “fun and empowering.”The foundation supported another group of Kansas City children just weeks earlier. On April 14, 2025, 15 and the Mahomies donated $15,000 to HALO’s Fresh Start Fund. The programme helped provide new wardrobes for 50 homeless children moving into HALO Homes in Kansas City.The donation covered basic items such as underwear, socks, shoes and clothing. For children entering a new home, those simple items can be some of the first things they get for themselves.HALO founder and CEO Rebecca Welsh explained the thinking behind the programme in the April 14 announcement.“Every child deserves to be confident. Every child deserves dignity,” Welsh said in HALO’s announcement of the Fresh Start Fund partnership.HALO also runs a Kansas City Learning Center that supports more than 700 homeless and at-risk children. Its services include tutoring, scholarships and life-skills programmes.The two projects show the range of Mahomes’ work with children in 2025. One focused on helping kids keep reading during the summer. The other helped homeless children settle into a new home with clothes and basic essentials.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes donated $15,000 to the Kansas City Public Library’s Summer Reading Program. The money helped the library purchase nearly 6,000 books for local children and support its effort to reduce summer learning loss. Mahomes also helped 50 homeless children get a fresh start with clothes and basic essentials.

Article Title: Indian Navy plans to procure six more landing craft utility platforms to boost amphibious operations
Article Text:
Indian Navy plans to procure six LCU Mk V vessels to boost amphibious, logistics and HADR capabilities.

NEW DELHI: To strengthen its amphibious operations, logistics and HADR capabilities, the Indian Navy is planning to procure six landing craft utility (LCU) MK V from Indian shipyards as it has issued a request for information (RFI) for six such platforms.A Landing Craft Utility (LCU) is a rugged, steel-hulled watercraft used by amphibious forces to transport heavy equipment, vehicles, and troops from ship to shore, along a coast, or back to warships. They are also used for humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, medical evacuation and specialized maritime operations.The Indian Navy currently has 8 active Landing Craft Utility (LCU) ships, all belonging to the indigenous Mk IV class. These amphibious ships displace about 830 tonnes and are primarily stationed under the Andaman and Nicobar Command for beaching, transport, and humanitarian missions. They can transport Main Battle Tanks (like Arjun or T-72), armoured vehicles, and up to 160 troops.According to the RFI, “The procurement of the vessel will be as per Defence Procurement Procedure 2.0, and accordingly shipyards are required to submit the details regarding indigenous content.The categorisation for the procurement is intended to be under Buy (Indian - IDDM).”Such a vessel with a displacement of 1,500 tonnes should be capable of carrying at least four main battle tanks (MBTs), 4 BMP infantry combat vehicles, and 190 troops and should have maximum speed of 15 knots or more with an endurance of around 4,500 nautical miles.“Shipyards may consider this RFI as advance information to obtain requisite govt clearances and setting up of necessary infrastructure both in terms of manpower and material requirements,” it said .
Article Summary: Indian Navy plans to procure six LCU Mk V vessels to boost amphibious, logistics and HADR capabilities. Landing Craft Utility (LCU) is a rugged, steel-hulled watercraft used by amphibious forces to transport heavy equipment, vehicles, and troops.

Article Title: Telangana SIR woes: Over 40 lakh hearing dates lapsed, 9L notices undelivered
Article Text:
Telangana's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls has experienced major delays in notice deliveries and hearings

‘Clear pendency’





HYDERABAD: With more than 40 lakh hearing dates already lapsed and over nine lakh notices yet to be delivered, Telangana’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls continues to face significant pendency, particularly in the Hyderabad metropolitan region, according to the latest status report released on Tuesday.Of the 92.88 lakh notices generated under the exercise, 83.72 lakh, or 90.1%, had been delivered as of 2 pm on Sept 22. However, the report showed that 40,77,727 hearing dates had lapsed, accounting for 43.9% of all notices generated. Another 55,462 rescheduled hearing dates had also lapsed. At the same time, around 46 lakh hearings had been completed.A major share of the remaining delivery backlog is concentrated in the Hyderabad metropolitan region. Rangareddy and Medchal Malkajgiri together accounted for 5.6 lakh of the 9.15 lakh undelivered notices statewide, representing nearly 61% of the total pendency. Rangareddy had 2.8 lakh notices yet to be delivered, while Medchal Malkajgiri had 2.7 lakh pending.At the Assembly constituency level, Serilingampally reported the highest number of pending notice deliveries at 1.1 lakh, followed by LB Nagar with 88,507 and Medchal with 80,932.While Hyderabad district recorded one of the highest delivery rates at 96.1%, another bottleneck emerged at the district election officer (DEO) verification stage. Of the 5.5 lakh cases pending with DEOs across the state, Hyderabad alone accounted for 3.4 lakh. The district also had 2.1 lakh cases pending for more than five days.Reviewing the exercise with DEOs, chief electoral officer C Sudharshan Reddy directed officials to expedite the disposal of anomaly and no-mapping cases and ensure that daily targets are met.He instructed officials to clear pending Forms 6, 7 and 8, along with hearing-related cases, while providing electors with adequate time to submit supporting documents. Cases pending at the electoral registration officer level should also be disposed of without delay, with additional computer operators deployed wherever necessary.The CEO said senior citizens and persons with disabilities should not be asked to attend hearings unnecessarily, while NRIs may submit documents through authorised representatives wherever applicable. He also directed officials to give special attention to ineligible voter cases and issue speaking orders after following due process.
Article Summary: Of 92.88 lakh notices generated under the exercise, 83.72 lakh, or 90.1%, had been delivered as of 2 pm on Sept 22. Rangareddy and Medchal Malkajgiri together accounted for 5.6 lakh of the 9.15 lakh undelivered notices statewide, representing nearly 61% of the total pendency.

Article Title: Telangana food safety crackdown: Houseflies, cockroaches found at dairies, FSSAI licences of 2 units suspended
Article Text:
Poor drainage and moss growth found during the searches





HYDERABAD: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) on Tuesday suspended the FSSAI licences of two dairy units in Rangareddy and ordered them to stop operations immediately after officials found serious hygiene and food-safety violations during a special inspection drive. The licences of Sapthagiri Foods at Karmanghat and All Rich Dairy in Pasumamula were suspended following the inspections.Separately, Venkata Shiva Milk Point in Hayathnagar was closed for operating without an FSSAI licence and under unhygienic conditions. Officials inspected 20 dairy establishments in Hyderabad’s core urban region and adjoining districts. As many as 18 samples were also collected from various units on suspicion of adulteration.At Sapthagiri Foods, officials found uneven flooring with moss growth, poor drainage, a heavy presence of houseflies, inadequate pest-control measures and garbage accumulation. Records of water and milk testing were also unavailable, while the hygiene practices of food handlers were found to be inadequate. At All Rich Dairy, officials reported housefly and cockroach infestation, slippery floors with water stagnation, inadequate lighting, spitting of pan masala inside the cold room and flaking of walls and ceilings.Personnel hygiene facilities were also found to be inadequate and unhygienic.TGSAFE said the two units had been directed to stop business operations immediately in the interest of public health. Officials also found mould growth, rusty equipment and pipes, poor drainage and a lack of water-testing, pest-control and health records of food handlers at some other establishments. Meanwhile, improvement notices will be issued to 10 such units, while show-cause notices will be issued to three others. A milk point at Hayathnagar was closed for operating without an FSSAI licence and under unhygienic conditions.
Article Summary: Sapthagiri Foods at Karmanghat and All Rich Dairy in Pasumamula were suspended following the inspections. Venkata Shiva Milk Point in Hayathnagar was closed for operating without an FSSAI licence and under unhygienic conditions.

Article Title: BMC seeks agency to diversify funding, explore alternative finance for infrastructure projects
Article Text:
BMC





MUMBAI: BMC is looking to appoint a project implementing agency to help it develop a broader financing strategy and mobilise funds through alternative sources for its growing infrastructure requirements, including water supply, wastewater, sanitation and urban infrastructure projects.The move comes as the BMC’s committed liabilities are are over Rs 2 lakh crores with major infrastructure projects like the Mumbai Coastal road -north, twin tunnels for Goregaon Mulund Link Road and the upgradation of sewage treatment plant underway.The civic body has invited e-tenders for an agency that will provide financial strategy, debt management and institutional coordination support, including identifying and structuring alternative financing options.According to the tender issued by the BMC’s Chief Accountant (Finance) on September 21, the selected agency will prepare a Capital Investment Plan (CIP) and a Debt Management Policy (DMP) and help the civic body mobilise funds through multiple financing instruments.The tender document states that BMC’s infrastructure requirements are growing in scale and complexity, creating a need to strengthen and diversify its financing capacity.The agency will be expected to identify projects that can attract financing, advise on financial structuring and help BMC access long-term capital on competitive terms.The proposed financing strategy will cover seven broad areas, including capital markets, climate and carbon finance, development finance, government support mechanisms, innovative and blended finance, and revenue enhancement measures.The agency will also advise BMC on municipal bonds, including green, sustainability, social and sustainability-linked bonds. Its mandate will include identifying opportunities for carbon credits, certification and monetisation, as well as helping the civic body access Central and state government grants, subsidies, low-interest loans and other schemes.BMC officials said it is separately in the process of appointing merchant bankers and other transaction intermediaries for specific assignments, including bond issuances. The proposed agency will therefore work alongside these intermediaries and provide end-to-end advisory, handholding, structuring and coordination support.An important part of the agency’s mandate will be to provide day-to-day support to BMC officials in their interactions with merchant bankers and other financial intermediaries, while also helping identify and structure additional sources of finance.“The agency will also assist the BMC Finance Department in preparing financial presentations, briefing notes and talking points for meetings with state government departments, external delegations, domestic and international study tours and apex bodies, including the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions,” states the tender document.
Article Summary: The civic body has invited e-tenders for an agency that will provide financial strategy, debt management and institutional coordination support. The agency will be expected to identify projects that can attract financing, advise on financial structuring and help BMC access long-term capital on competitive terms.

MUMBAI: The BMC’s proposal to increase theatre tax on cinema halls and other entertainment venues is still awaiting approval from the state government’s Urban Development (UD) Department, civic officials said. Until the revised rates are sanctioned and notified, only the existing rates will apply, officials said.The civic administration has proposed retaining the existing 2014-15 rates for 2027-28 until the state government approves the revised rates and issues a notification in the Official Gazette.The proposed revision, pending with the UD department, could see the tax on multiplex cinemas increase to Rs 400 per show from the existing Rs 60 for air-conditioned cinemas. The proposal provides for a tax of Rs 200 per show for single-screen AC cinemas, Rs 90 for non-AC cinemas, and Rs 100 per show for drama, jalsa and other entertainment programmes.Tajinder Tiwana, a law committee member, said the proposal was discussed in detail during the law committee meeting held on Tuesday and would be deliberated further.The BMC has been pursuing approval of the revised rates with the state government.According to the civic proposal, the revised rates will come into force only from the date specified by the state government in its Gazette notification.“For now, the old rates will continue to apply as the revised rates are yet to be sanctioned by the Urban Development Department,” a BMC official said.Under the existing rates, an AC cinema is charged Rs 60 per show and a non-AC cinema Rs 45 per show. Drama and other entertainment programmes attract Rs 25 per show, while circuses and funfairs are taxed at Rs 50 per day.The BMC has also proposed continuing the exemption from theatre tax for Marathi and Gujarati films, plays, one-act plays and tamashas, irrespective of the category of theatre.The 6% concession available since 1959 to taxpayers who pay their monthly theatre tax in advance by the fifth of the month is also proposed to continue for 2027-28.The annual theatre tax rates for 2027-28 will require approval from the Law Committee, Standing Committee and the Municipal Corporation.
Article Summary: The BMC’s proposal to increase theatre tax on cinema halls and other entertainment venues is still awaiting approval from the state government. Until the revised rates are sanctioned and notified, only the existing rates will apply, officials said. The proposed revision could see the tax on multiplex cinemas increase to Rs 400 per show.

Article Title: 'RERA carpet area of 63,000 square feet': Angel One founder Dinesh Thakkar buys Juhu tower for Rs 711 crore
Article Text:
(Image Credit: Instagram) Dinesh Thakkar, founder, chairman and managing director of Angel One Ltd (AOL)





MUMBAI: Embassy Developments Ltd on Tuesday announced it signed a MoU for the sale of an entire residential tower at its ultra-luxury development, Embassy Terazza, in Juhu to Dinesh Thakkar, founder, chairman and managing director of Angel One Ltd (AOL) for Rs 711 crore.The residence comprises an entire ground-plus-seven-storey tower with a RERA carpet area of 63,000 square feet.Located on Juhu Tara Road, the developer said the project is an “ultra-luxury low-density development” spanning more than two acres with approximately 50 residences and has an estimated gross development value (GDV) in excess of Rs 3,000 crore. Design features include one residence per floor across the five towers.Thakkar said, “Juhu has always had a special character that very few locations in Mumbai can match. When I started looking for a new home, my focus was on privacy, spaciousness, exceptional sea views and creating a luxurious, iconic sanctuary that would become our family home.”In 2021, DMart founder Radhakishan Damani purchased a bungalow property at Narayan Dabholkar Road in south Mumbai for a record Rs 1,001 crore. The bungalow called Madhu Kunj is located on prime 1.5-acre land with a built-up area of more than 60,000 square feet in tony Malabar Hill. And in 2023, 23 luxury apartments in a residential project in Worli were bought by the family, relatives, friends and close associates of Damani for around Rs 1,200 crore. The luxury apartments were in Tower B of Three Sixty West on Dr Annie Besant Road.
Article Summary: The residence comprises an entire ground-plus-seven-storey tower with a RERA carpet area of 63,000 square feet. The developer said the project is an “ultra- luxury low-density development’ spanning more than two acres with approximately 50 residences.
